questions.question_text:
A column graph has a title, labelled axes and equally spaced tick marks on its vertical frequency axis numbered $0, 2, 4, 6, 10, 12$. All columns use the same colour to show one group.
Which graph convention does this break?

options.text: Equal numerical increments must correspond to equal physical intervals
The frequency scale must start at $0$
options.why: The scale already starts at $0$; this overlooks the uneven jump from $6$ to $10$.
Both axes are already labelled; this confuses axis labels with the numerical scale.

options.text: A key must explain colours used for different groups
options.why: The columns show only one group in one colour; this assumes that every column graph needs a key.

questions.solution_text:
The steps are $2, 2, 2, 4, 2$, so the jump from $6$ to $10$ is uneven despite the tick marks being equally spaced.
Equal numerical increments must correspond to equal physical intervals.

questions.question_text:
A column graph compares two teams using green and orange bars, but nothing tells the reader what each colour represents.
Which convention is missing?

options.why: A title names the whole graph; it would not say which colour is which team.
The scale is unrelated to explaining what the two colours mean.
A source says where the data came from, not what each colour represents.

questions.solution_text:
Two colours stand for two teams, so the reader must be told which colour is which.
A key (legend) is missing.

questions.question_text:
A column graph has a horizontal axis labelled "Method of transport" with categories car, bus, walk, bike and other. Its vertical axis is labelled "Number of students", with an even scale starting at $0$. The columns show $28, 36, 12, 18$ and $6$ students respectively.
Which is a relevant title for this graph?

options.text: Students' methods of transport to school
Time students take to travel to school
options.why: This treats the student counts as travel times, although the vertical axis measures the number of students.
This mistakes students' transport categories for a count of passing vehicles; walking is also included.
This ignores the horizontal categories, which are methods of transport rather than school subjects.

questions.solution_text:
The categories are methods of transport and the columns count students.
A relevant title is "Students' methods of transport to school".
